description.main: A collaboration from Artspace Books' artist-and-writer series: twenty-one colour photographs by Jack Pierson paired with a short work of fiction by Jim Lewis, made on a road trip from Hollywood to Las Vegas. Published in San Francisco in 1993 as a small hardcover in photo-illustrated boards with no dust jacket. This copy is the first edition, first printing.
description.extended:
A road-trip book from Artspace Books' artist-and-writer series, Real Gone (San Francisco, 1993) pairs twenty-one colour photographs by Jack Pierson (b. 1960) with a short work of fiction by the novelist Jim Lewis about a drive from Hollywood to Las Vegas.

The publisher calls it the tale of a crazy road trip. Lewis writes the story as a letter. Two travellers leave Hollywood, cross paths with an ex-lawyer named Hoyt and a run of oddballs, and end up arrested for driving a stolen car. The Library of Congress files the book as fiction, under Las Vegas and city and town life. It is a small hardcover, 6 by 8 inches, in photo-illustrated boards with no dust jacket as issued. This copy is the first edition, first printing.

Pierson, born in Plymouth, Massachusetts, works across photography, drawing, sculpture and word sculptures built from letters salvaged from marquees and Las Vegas casinos. The Irish Museum of Modern Art gave him a retrospective in 2008. Lewis (b. 1963) published his first novel, Sister, the same year as this book. The library also holds Pierson's Tomorrow's Man 1 to 6, The Hungry Years, Jesus and Nazimova, Andre, Array (Miami Beach), It's Not Dark Yet and the Photology monograph.
description.artist_bio: Jack Pierson (b. 1960, Plymouth, Massachusetts) lives and works in New York and California, working across photography, drawing, sculpture and word sculptures built from salvaged letters. Collections include the Metropolitan Museum of Art, the Guggenheim, LACMA and the ICA Boston; retrospective at the Irish Museum of Modern Art, 2008 (Xavier Hufkens). Jim Lewis (b. 1963, Cleveland) is the author of the novels Sister (Graywolf, 1993), Why the Tree Loves the Ax (Crown, 1998), The King is Dead (Knopf, 2003) and Ghosts of New York (WVU Press, 2021); collaborated with Cecily Brown on The English Garden (Karma, 2015) (Wikipedia).
